purpose: Harden the GitHub Actions release adapter so registry publication and repository mutation occur only through a narrowly authorized, reviewable release boundary.
scope: .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml and its referenced actions, GitHub Environment configuration documentation, action pinning, permissions, artifact handoff, and workflow tests.
non_goals: Making GitHub Actions the only supported CI or release platform.
Moving provider-neutral release rules from callisto core into workflow shell code.
Requiring Git tag signing in this track; signature policy is covered by SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The workflow implements the plan-job to execute-job topology defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001: unprivileged verification/planning is a separate job from privileged release execution. Only the execute job can receive registry credentials or write tags/releases, and it is bound to a named GitHub Environment. The repository documents the environment name, required reviewers, and branch/tag deployment rules plus an administrator-verifiable API or console procedure; workflow YAML reference alone is explicitly insufficient evidence that protection rules exist. Non-release jobs receive neither registry secrets nor write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN permissions.

Each workflow and job declares the least GitHub token permissions it needs. contents, pull-requests, checks, and statuses are write-scoped only in the job that demonstrably performs that operation; all other jobs default to read or none. A workflow test or policy check rejects an unscoped top-level write grant.

Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable full commit SHAs. A nearby comment records the upstream tag or release used for human review. CI verifies the pin format and fails if an external action reference is changed to a mutable tag or branch.

The planning job uploads the explicit durable plan from SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001 and exposes its artifact identifier and envelope digest. The protected release job downloads only that identifier from its own workflow run, verifies its digest and source_commit against its checkout, then invokes core plan validation before credentials are used. Caches may accelerate dependency installation but are never read as release intent.

Changes to .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ require CODEOWNERS review from the release-security owners. The release trigger and environment policy document exactly which events may create a version PR, which may publish, who approves publication, and how an emergency rerun is reconciled. The privileged execute job is reachable only from an explicit protected-ref release dispatch/reusable-workflow contract, never from a normal push to main; workflow-code changes in that push cannot grant registry publication authority.
